title: Team Access Escalation via AuthorizedResourceControlUpdate Logic Flaw
summary:
## Summary

Portainer uses **resource controls** to restrict which users and teams can see and manage a given resource - a stack, container, volume, service, config, or secret. A logic flaw in the resource-control update authorization (`AuthorizedResourceControlUpdate`) lets a non-administrative user grant access to a resource they control to teams they do not belong to. Any authenticated user who already controls a resource, either through team-based access or as its owner, can exploit this through the standard access-management UI or the `PUT /api/resource_controls/{id}` endpoint.

The authorization check is meant to confirm that the caller is a member of every team being added to a resource control, and that a non-administrator does not mix user and team accesses. Two code paths in the check returned success before the full team list was validated. In the first, the check returned as soon as it found a single team the caller belongs to. In the second, a payload containing the caller's own user access together with two or more teams returned success on the user access alone, and the team list was never examined.

The update handler applies the submitted access lists to the resource control *before* running the authorization check, so the check operates on the already-mutated lists. The result is a horizontal access-control bypass across team boundaries: resources that resource controls are meant to isolate can be exposed to arbitrary teams within the same Portainer instance.

An earlier release addressed the first path only. This advisory covers both, and the fix in the releases listed below is complete for both.

## Severity

**Medium**

Exploitation is achievable over the network through a single authenticated API call, with low attack complexity and no user interaction. It does require a pre-existing account that already controls the target resource, so privileges required are low rather than none. The impact is contained to Portainer's own access-control model: an attacker can break the confidentiality and integrity of resource isolation by exposing resources they control to unauthorized teams, who then gain the ability to view and manage those resources. The flaw does not by itself grant the attacker new access to resources owned by others, nor does it directly compromise the underlying host or managed environments, which keeps the subsequent-system impact limited and the overall rating at Medium.

## Affected Versions

The flaw exists in the original ResourceControl authorization logic and is present in every supported release prior to the complete fix.

Portainer Community Edition and Portainer Business Edition share release version numbering; the table below applies to both editions.

Portainer 2.45.2 contains the complete fix. A fix for the 2.39.x LTS line has been merged and will ship in a future 2.39.x release; this advisory will be updated when it does.

| Branch              | First vulnerable | Fixed in                                        |
|---------------------|------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| 2.39.x (LTS)        | 2.39.0           | Not yet patched - upgrade to **2.45.2** or later |
| 2.40.x-2.44.x (STS) | 2.40.0           | Out of support - upgrade to **2.45.2** or later  |
| 2.45.x (LTS)        | 2.45.0           | **2.45.2**                                      |

Releases 2.39.3 and 2.43.0 and later contain the fix for the first path only; they remain affected by the second path. Users on the 2.39.x LTS line, on any 2.40.x-2.44.x STS release, or on end-of-life versions prior to 2.39.0 should upgrade to 2.45.2 or later.

## Workarounds

Administrators who cannot immediately upgrade can reduce exposure by:

- **Auditing resource-control team assignments.** Review the team accesses on existing resource controls for teams that should not have access, paying particular attention to sensitive stacks, secrets, and configs.
